_about: Input to build_election_calendar.py: each state's (and D.C.'s) voter deadlines for the general election, as its election authority or its statute states them. Each item cites the page that says so, with a passage quoted verbatim (as the script's --text normalises it) so the script can confirm the page still says it. Sources are the state's own pages or statute, never an aggregator; a page behind a bot wall is never worked around (AGENTS.md section 7): cite the statute, or leave the item out, since the script refuses an item it cannot verify. A state with no readable official source carries `unread` (why, never served) and no items. Researched 2026-10-12/13. A state's `_research` (never served) says how its items were sourced. Edit an item, then rerun the script. `register` names the state's page for registering to vote (its online registration where it has one, else its registration page); the script checks it answers on the state's own domain, and a page behind a bot wall is kept but marked unconfirmed. `none` with a quote states a state has no registration. `registerFallback` is vote.gov, for a state with no entry.
